rows: This document contains easy formatted text that you can copy/paste for writing offers or specifying Woodward
power management products for your project.

The power generation system shall be controlled by a microprocessor based power management system consisting of
Woodward easYgen-3100XT/3200XT-P1 series controller on each generator source. The generator controllers shall operate in
a peer-to-peer system with up to 32 synchronous or asynchronous generators. This system will provide automatic sequencing
of multiple units, synchronization, generator and utility breaker control, soft loading and unloading for bumpless transfers, real
KW load control, reactive KVAR or power factor control, metering, communications and diagnostic features. The generator
controller shall be a commercially available control and not PLC based, and shall be configured for operation without the need
for customized, proprietary programming or software. The system shall be able to be configured either in a simple island
arrangement or in a system with up to one utility intertie and multiple generators. Specific requirements are as follows:
|  | Automatically starts and stops generator sets upon utility failure or utility restoration.
|  | Automatically starts and stops generator sets based on plant load to maintain the power interchange at the utility intertie
|  | Automatic generator set loading and unloading for soft transfer
|  | Automatic load dependent start/stop for improved generator system efficiency with configurable generator priority
sequencing based on generator size, service hours, fuel efficiency or fixed sequence.
|  | Applications with up to 32 generator sets and one utility tie in the system.
|  | Independent phase match or slip frequency synchronization with voltage matching for control of generator and
|  | Dead bus closing logic internal to the controller to ensure multiple units close safely within the synchronization
|  | Breaker or contactor control for generators.
|  | RMS measurement of voltage and current for reduced susceptibility to harmonics.
|  | Speed bias signal to prime mover speed control freely configurable in the range of +/- 20 ma, +/- 10 volts, or 0-10 VDC,
500 Hz PWM, and discrete raise/lower to control prime movers of different types (diesel engine, gaseous or bio-fueled
|  | Configurable load and unload ramp rates for generators or the entire system at the utility tie.
|  | Proportional load sharing (isochronous or droop) of up to 32 generators, regardless of KW rating.
|  | Import/export control at the utility mains breaker.
|  | Externally adjustable load or process references using analog inputs, Ethernet or Serial Modbus RTU (slave), CAN
|  | Digital load sharing integral to the controller without external load sharing control modules.
|  | Voltage bias signal to AVR freely configurable in the range of +/- 20 mA, +/- 10 V, or 0..10 VDC, 500 Hz PWM, and
|  | VAR sharing on isolated buses using percentage base reactive load sharing
|  | Configurable load and unload ramp rates for generators, or the entire system at the utility ties.
|  | VAR/PF control in process, base load, or import/export control.
|  | Externally adjustable VAR or PF references using analog inputs, Ethernet or Serial Modbus RTU (slave), CAN open.
|  | Configurable start and stop logic for diesel and gas engines with
|  | CAN SAE J1939 network communication/control to engine ECU.
|  | Customizable protection based upon J1939 or analog inputs.
|  | Phase over current instantaneous (ANSI | 50) and time
|  | Phase over current with voltage restraint | (ANSI 51V)
|  | Voltage RMS 0.5% accuracy—L-N, L-L, average; 1-phase or 3-phase generator and mains, 1-phase load bus.
|  | Current RMS 0.5% accuracy—Line current and average; 1-phase or 3-phase generator, 1-phase mains
|  | Power RMS 1.0% accuracy—kVA, kVAR and kW per phase and total; PF per phase and average; total generator
|  | The generator controller shall be able to select either CAN bus or Ethernet communication interface which allows
control and operation of the complete system.
|  | CAN SAE J1939 network communications to engine ECU.
|  | Ethernet and Serial Modbus RTU (slave) communication for SCADA annunciation and external control.
|  | Connectivity with the Remote Panel for complete annunciation, control and configuration of the generator controllers,
|  | Configuration via USB or Ethernet to PC/laptop with Woodward Toolkit service tool.
|  | Design allows operation with one or more system node failures. Controller will provide a missing member alarm, which
will allow the system, if programmed accordingly, to go from isochronous to droop load sharing for continued operation.
|  | Configuration Check in Load Dependent Start/Stop
|  | Breaker/Contactor synchronization time out and reclose alarms
|  | Analog input out of range alarms
|  | Sequence of events recorder—300 events FIFO with real time clock.
|  | Graphical overview of generators and mains on easYgen-3200XT and RP-3000XT Remote Panel.
|  | The door mounted generator controller shall have sealed soft keys and a large, easy-to-read backlit color LCD, with a
graphical display and text that can configured in 14 languages.
|  | The back panel mounted generator controller shall be encased in a rugged aluminum chassis. Back panel mounting
decreases wiring to the door, and may eliminate the need for voltage transformers to keep dangerous voltages away
|  | The door mounted remote control and annunciation panel can be used with either the back panel mounted generator
controller or the door mounted generator controller. The remote panel provides control from the front panel (door),
reduces wiring to the door, and keeps high voltage connections on the back panel if used with the back panel mounted
controller. Each remote panel can communicate with one or more generator controllers.
